processing: Fully oxidised orthodox black tea, sold in grades from broken GFBOP up to tippy TGFOP1 and SFTGFOP1.
harvest_season: Sold by year; no garden-specific calendar is documented. As with other Assam gardens, the May to June second flush is generally the most valued.
appearance_dry: Dark leaf with golden tips in the higher grades, smaller broken leaf in GFBOP.
appearance_liquor: Reddish brown, as is usual for Assam orthodox.
appearance_wet: Coppery leaf, whole or broken according to grade.
taste_profile: A hearty, malty Assam with a full body, by sellers' accounts; opinions on individual lots vary, so taste before buying much.

brewing.notes: Start at three minutes for broken grades, four for tippy ones. Add milk if the cup is too brisk for you.

vintage_note: Importers list it by year and grade, such as a 2026 TGFOP1, so the season is usually easy to check. As usual for Assam, buy the latest lot you can find and drink it within a year or two.
description:
Hattialli is an Assam estate that importers list under Dibrugarh. It is known mainly through the import trade, and it appears alongside better-known gardens in shop lists of notable Assam estates.

It is sold in orthodox grades. These run from a broken GFBOP, which gives a strong cup fast, to tippy grades with more golden bud and a softer finish.

Expect a hearty, malty Assam rather than anything delicate. Reports differ: importers praise it, while one independent reviewer of a GTGFOP lot found it fairly bland. So try a small amount from any new season first.

Do not confuse it with Hathikuli, an organic Assam estate near Kaziranga with a similar-sounding name. The spelling Hathialli also appears for this garden, so check the label before comparing notes.
history: Little is documented about this garden's founding or ownership. Its visible record is commercial: importer listings under the spelling Hattialli.
